issues.legal_issue: Taking actual possession of acquired land vests it in the government and prevents withdrawal from the acquisition.
material_facts: After an award was made, the authorities notified the co-owners to attend the taking of possession; two co-owners attended.
The acquiring officer took possession in the presence of witnesses and prepared a signed panchnama recording it.
The government’s name was entered in the revenue records, and it later handed possession to the development authority, whose name was also entered in those records.
issues.conclusion: The government had taken possession in accordance with law, so the land vested absolutely in it free from encumbrances.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 11 and 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, possession taken after an award vests the land absolutely in the government. Possession must be actual, not merely symbolic or recorded on paper; what act suffices depends on the nature of the land. The Court applied the majority reasoning in Balwant Narayan Bhagde v. M.D. Bhagwat, (1976) 1 SCC 700.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the acquisition of land by the government.
predicates.award_made: The acquiring authority made an award for the land.
predicates.actual_possession_taken: The authorities actually took possession of the land, rather than merely recording symbolic or paper possession.

issues.definition: When an award has been made in a land-acquisition proceeding and the government actually takes possession, the land vests absolutely in the government.

issues.legal_issue: The government cannot withdraw acquired land after taking possession, and its minister has no power to order such a withdrawal.
material_facts: The authorities had taken possession of the land and the land had vested in the government.
A minister later directed that the land be deleted from the acquisition proceedings.
issues.conclusion: Section 48 did not apply after possession had been taken, and the minister had no power to order release of the land from acquisition.
issues.legal_principle: Section 48(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 permits the government to withdraw from acquisition only where possession has not been taken, subject to the exception stated in that section. Under Section 16, taking possession after an award vests the land absolutely in the government. The Court relied on the possession test in Balwant Narayan Bhagde v. M.D. Bhagwat, (1976) 1 SCC 700.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns land acquired by the government.
predicates.actual_possession_taken: The government actually took possession of the acquired land.
predicates.minister_sought_withdrawal: A minister acting for the government sought or directed withdrawal of the land from acquisition.

issues.definition: If a minister seeks withdrawal of acquired land in a land-acquisition proceeding after the government has actually taken possession, the government cannot withdraw the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: An unapproved or uncommunicated government file noting does not create an enforceable right to release land from acquisition.
material_facts: The minister made a noting in a government file directing release of the land.
The noting was not communicated to the landowners and the government later directed fresh consideration of matters whose orders had not been communicated.
The landowners sought a mandamus requiring the government to give effect to the noting.
issues.conclusion: The noting was not a legal order and created no right that could be enforced by mandamus.
issues.legal_principle: A file noting is an internal expression of opinion, not a government decision creating rights. A decision must be approved by the competent authority and communicated to the affected person; it must also be expressed and authenticated as required by Article 166 of the Constitution. The Court relied on State of Punjab v. Sodhi Sukhdev Singh, AIR 1961 SC 493; State of Bihar v. Kripalu Shankar, (1987) 3 SCC 34; Rajasthan Housing Board v. Shri Krishan, (1993) 2 SCC 84; Sethi Auto Service Station v. DDA, (2009) 1 SCC 180; and Shanti Sports Club v. Union of India, (2009) 15 SCC 705.

rule.if: mandamus_proceeding and government_file_noting_exists and (not approved_by_competent_authority or not communicated_to_affected_person)

predicates.mandamus_proceeding: A person seeks a court order compelling the government to act on its decision.
predicates.government_file_noting_exists: A direction or view concerning the person’s matter appears only as a noting in a government file.
predicates.approved_by_competent_authority: The competent government authority approved the decision in the required manner.
predicates.communicated_to_affected_person: The government communicated the decision to the person affected by it.

issues.definition: In a proceeding seeking mandamus, a government file noting that lacks competent approval or communication to the affected person creates no enforceable right.

issues.legal_issue: Withdrawal from land acquisition is complete only when the government issues a notification in the official gazette.
material_facts: The minister made a file noting directing release of the land, but the government did not issue a notification in the official gazette releasing it.
The landowners sought a direction requiring the government to implement the noting.
issues.conclusion: The noting did not complete withdrawal from acquisition; a notification in the official gazette was required.
issues.legal_principle: Although Section 48(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 does not expressly prescribe a mode of withdrawal, the scheme of the Act requires withdrawal to be effected by an official-gazette notification. The Court relied on Shanti Sports Club v. Union of India, (2009) 15 SCC 705, including its discussion of Municipal Committee, Bhatinda v. Land Acquisition Collector, (1993) 3 SCC 24; U.P. State Sugar Corporation Ltd. v. State of U.P., (1995) Supp 3 SCC 538; State of Maharashtra v. Umashankar Rajabhau, (1996) 1 SCC 299; and State of T.N. v. L. Krishnan, (1996) 7 SCC 450.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and withdrawal_from_acquisition_proposed and not official_gazette_notification_issued

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns land acquired by the government.
predicates.withdrawal_from_acquisition_proposed: The government has proposed to withdraw land from acquisition.
predicates.official_gazette_notification_issued: The government has issued an official-gazette notification effecting withdrawal from acquisition.

issues.definition: A proposed withdrawal from acquisition is not completed unless the government issues an official-gazette notification.

issues.legal_issue: A landowner cannot relitigate an issue already finally decided against it, and a partial release made as part of a bargain does not entitle it to demand further release.
material_facts: Earlier proceedings concerning whether the remaining acquired land should be released were decided against the landowners, including proceedings that reached the Supreme Court.
After part of the land was released and the remaining land was retained for the development project, the landowners brought another proceeding seeking further release.
The Court regarded the earlier partial release and retention as a bargain.
issues.conclusion: The earlier final decisions bound the parties and prevented the landowners from raising the same issue again; the partial release also disentitled them from seeking further release.
issues.legal_principle: Final decisions bind the parties and prevent repeated litigation of the same issue. The Court also held that the partial release and retention of the remaining land for the project constituted a bargain that disentitled the landowners from seeking further release.

predicates.writ_petition_after_prior_final_litigati: A person brings a writ petition after earlier litigation concerning the same land has ended in a final decision.
predicates.same_issue_reasserted: The later proceeding again seeks a determination of an issue already decided in the earlier litigation.
predicates.partial_release_was_part_of_bargain: The government released part of the land while retaining the remainder for the project as part of a bargain with the landowners.

issues.definition: A later writ petition reasserting an issue finally decided in earlier litigation is barred where the partial release and retention of the remaining land formed part of a bargain.
